stemMd: A secreted protein acquires a carbohydrate chain in the ER lumen. After its vesicle fuses with the plasma membrane, on which side of the membrane is that carbohydrate exposed?

options.label: E
options.textMd: It must be removed before fusion.

explanationMd: The lumen of an ER-derived secretory vesicle is topologically continuous with the extracellular space after exocytosis. Membrane fusion preserves orientation, so luminal carbohydrate faces outward.

distractorRationale.c: Nuclear pores do not carry the secretory vesicle lumen.
distractorRationale.e: Glycosylation need not be removed during secretion.
distractorRationale.a: Mitochondria are outside this secretory route.
distractorRationale.b: The vesicle lumen does not become the cytosol.
